_about: Treatment knowledge for the 38 PlantVillage classes. Keys match the model's class_names.json. Chemical doses are typical label rates for products commonly registered in India: always follow the product label and local advisories.
chemical_disclaimer: Use chemicals only as per the product label, wear gloves and a mask, keep children and animals away, and respect the waiting period before harvest. Confirm with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra / agriculture officer before spraying.

Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; infected fruit becomes cracked and deformed; leaves may yellow and drop early.
organic: Collect and destroy fallen leaves to reduce overwintering spores
Spray wettable sulphur or a Bordeaux mixture (1%) at green-tip stage
Prune to open the canopy for better air flow
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L, repeat at 10-14 day intervals in wet weather
Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1 ml/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L once infection is seen
prevention: Apply urea (5%) on fallen leaves in autumn to speed decomposition

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered 'frog-eye' spots on leaves; brown to black rot on fruit, often starting at the blossom end; sunken cankers on branches.
organic: Prune out dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit and burn them
Spray copper-based fungicide or Bordeaux mixture (1%) during the season
chemical: Captan 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L from petal fall at 10-14 day intervals
Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L for heavy infection
prevention: Remove fruit mummies from trees and ground
Keep trees vigorous with balanced nutrition

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface, later with small tube-like structures underneath; fruit may show orange lesions.
organic: Remove nearby juniper / cedar host plants or their galls
Spray wettable sulphur 80% WP @ 2 g/L at early leaf stage
chemical: Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1 ml/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L from pink bud stage, 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L as protectant
prevention: Keep apple orchards away from junipers
Begin protective sprays before symptoms in rainy springs

Apple___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue regular compost / FYM application
Keep monitoring weekly, especially after rain
prevention: Clean up fallen leaves and fruit

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Maintain acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) with organic mulch such as pine needles or sawdust
prevention: Water at the base, not on leaves
Remove weak or dead canes every year

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves and shoots; leaves curl upward and may become brittle; fruit can show white growth.
organic: Spray wettable sulphur 80% WP @ 2-3 g/L (not in very hot weather)
Potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L) or neem oil (3-5 ml/L) sprays
Prune crowded shoots to improve air flow
chemical: Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1 ml/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.5 g/L, 2-3 sprays at 10-14 day intervals

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Mulch with compost and keep the tree base weed-free
prevention: Watch for white powder on young leaves during humid spells

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey to tan lesions running between leaf veins; lesions merge and leaves dry out from the bottom up.
organic: Rotate with a non-cereal crop for at least one season
Plough under or remove infected crop residue
Spray Trichoderma- or Pseudomonas-based biofungicide at early stage
chemical: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1 ml/L, or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L at first symptoms
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L as protectant
prevention: Avoid continuous maize on the same field
Maintain proper plant spacing for air flow

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, raised, reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces; heavy infection turns leaves yellow and dry.
organic: Remove volunteer maize plants and weed hosts
Spray neem oil (3-5 ml/L) at early stage to slow spread
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at first pustules, repeat after 10-15 days
Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L for severe cases
prevention: Sow at the recommended time to avoid cool, humid periods during early growth

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long (2.5-15 cm), cigar-shaped, grey-green to tan lesions on leaves, starting on lower leaves; severe blight dries the whole leaf.
organic: Deep ploughing to bury infected residue
Crop rotation with pulses or oilseeds
Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at first symptoms, 2 sprays at 10-day intervals
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 ml/L for heavy infection

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue FYM / compost and timely weeding
prevention: Scout weekly for leaf spots and fall armyworm

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Brown circular leaf spots with dark borders and black dots; berries turn brown, then shrivel into hard black 'mummies'.
organic: Remove and destroy mummified berries and infected canes
Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) from early shoot growth
Improve canopy air flow by shoot thinning
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L as protectant from early shoot stage
Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.4 g/L or Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1 ml/L at bloom and early berry stage
prevention: Sanitation: clear all mummies before the new season

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' yellow or red patches between leaf veins that dry out; small dark spots on berries; wood shows dark streaks; vines may collapse suddenly.
organic: Cut out and burn infected arms and trunks well below the affected wood
Apply Trichoderma-based wound protectant on pruning cuts
chemical: No curative spray exists. Protect large pruning wounds with a fungicidal paste (e.g. copper oxychloride paste) right after pruning
prevention: Prune in dry weather and disinfect tools

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots on older leaves, which dry and fall early; severe infection weakens the vine.
organic: Remove infected leaves and fallen debris
Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper hydroxide
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L at 10-15 day intervals
Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1 g/L for severe infection
prevention: Clean up leaf litter after pruning

Grape___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue compost application and canopy management
prevention: Scout after rains for downy and powdery mildew

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter), spread by the citrus psyllid insect
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellow mottling on leaves (not symmetric like nutrient deficiency); small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green; twig dieback.
organic: Remove and destroy infected trees to stop spread
Spray neem oil (5 ml/L) to suppress psyllids
Use yellow sticky traps to monitor psyllids
chemical: There is no cure. Control the psyllid vector: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L during new flush
prevention: Control psyllids during every new leaf flush
Apply zinc and micronutrient sprays to keep trees vigorous

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn purple-black and fall out, leaving 'shot holes'; pitted, cracked spots on fruit.
organic: Spray copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture (1%) at leaf fall and bud swell
Remove badly infected twigs
chemical: Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (100 ppm), 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals
prevention: Plant windbreaks, since windblown sand injures leaves and spreads bacteria

Peach___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue balanced organic manuring
prevention: Watch for leaf spots after warm rains

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown with yellow halos; leaves drop; raised, scabby spots on fruit.
organic: Use hot-water treated seed (50 °C for 25 min)
Remove infected plants and debris
Spray copper hydroxide at first symptoms
chemical: Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (100 ppm), at 7-10 day intervals in wet weather
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and seedlings
Rotate away from tomato and pepper for 2-3 years
Avoid overhead irrigation and working in wet fields

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Mulch to keep soil moisture even and leaves clean
prevention: Watch for thrips, mites and leaf curl

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric 'target-board' rings on older leaves, often with a yellow halo; leaves dry from the bottom up.
organic: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
Spray Trichoderma- or Bacillus subtilis-based biofungicide
Mulch to prevent soil splash
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L at first symptoms, repeat every 10-12 days
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 ml/L for heavy infection
prevention: Balanced nutrition, since weak plants are more susceptible

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Pale green, water-soaked patches that quickly turn dark brown-black, with white fungal growth underneath in humid weather; tubers show brown rot. Spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately (do not compost)
Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) preventively in cool, cloudy, humid weather
Earth up the rows to protect tubers
chemical: Preventive: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L
After symptoms: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 3 g/L; repeat after 7-10 days if the weather stays wet
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed tubers and resistant varieties
Destroy cull piles and volunteer potato plants

Potato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue earthing up and organic manuring
prevention: In cool, foggy weather, scout daily for late blight

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Mulch and apply compost each season
prevention: Remove old fruited canes after harvest
Keep rows narrow for air flow

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Rhizobium + PSB seed treatment at sowing
prevention: Watch for yellow mosaic and rust during humid weather

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery spots on leaves and stems that spread to cover the leaf; leaves yellow, dry and die early, reducing yield.
organic: Spray wettable sulphur 80% WP @ 2 g/L (avoid in very hot weather)
Milk spray (1 part milk : 9 parts water) or potassium bicarbonate (5 g/L)
Neem oil 3-5 ml/L
chemical: Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 1 ml/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 0.5 g/L, 2-3 sprays at 10-day intervals
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L
prevention: Give plants enough space and sunlight

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small, irregular purple spots on leaves; spots merge and leaf edges dry, so leaves look scorched.
organic: Remove and destroy infected leaves after harvest
Spray copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture (0.5-1%)
chemical: Captan 50% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2 g/L at 10-14 day intervals during wet weather
prevention: Use drip irrigation and straw mulch

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Straw mulch to keep fruit off the soil

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves, often with yellow halos; spots on fruit are raised and scabby.
organic: Use hot-water treated seed (50 °C for 25 min)
Remove infected leaves and plants
Spray copper hydroxide at first symptoms
chemical: Copper oxychloride 50% WP @ 3 g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1 g/L (100 ppm), at 7-10 day intervals

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, with yellowing around them; dark sunken areas at the stem end of fruit.
organic: Remove lower infected leaves
Mulch to prevent soil splash
Spray Trichoderma- or Bacillus subtilis-based biofungicide
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L every 7-10 days
Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L for heavy infection
prevention: Stake plants and prune lower leaves for air flow

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular, greasy grey-green to brown patches on leaves, with white growth underneath in humid weather; firm brown rot on fruit. Spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) preventively in cool, humid weather
chemical: Preventive: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L
After symptoms: Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 3 g/L, repeat after 7-10 days
prevention: Do not plant near potato fields

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on the upper leaf surface with olive-green to grey velvety mould underneath; mostly in humid greenhouses / polyhouses.
organic: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity
Remove infected leaves
Spray copper hydroxide or Bacillus subtilis-based biofungicide
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L at 7-10 day intervals
prevention: Keep relative humidity below 85% in protected cultivation

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small, round spots with dark borders and grey-white centres containing tiny black dots, starting on lower leaves; leaves yellow and fall.
organic: Remove infected lower leaves
Mulch to stop soil splash
Spray copper-based fungicide
chemical: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L every 7-10 days during wet weather
prevention: Crop rotation for at least 1-2 years

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow-white speckling on leaves, later bronze and dry; fine webbing on the leaf underside; worse in hot, dry weather.
organic: Spray a strong water jet on the leaf underside
Neem oil 3-5 ml/L or neem seed kernel extract (5%)
Encourage natural predators such as predatory mites and ladybird beetles
chemical: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L or Fenpyroximate 5% EC @ 1 ml/L, sprayed on the leaf underside; rotate products to avoid resistance
prevention: Keep plants well watered, since stressed plants attract mites
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with light centres and concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit; leaves drop when severe.
organic: Remove infected leaves and crop debris
Improve air flow by pruning and staking
chemical: Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2 g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1 ml/L at 7-14 day intervals
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L as protectant
prevention: Avoid dense planting and excess nitrogen

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward, become small, thick and yellow at the edges; plants are stunted and bushy; very few fruits set.
organic: Uproot and destroy infected plants early
Yellow sticky traps (10-12 per acre) to trap whiteflies
Neem oil 5 ml/L to repel whiteflies
Grow seedlings under insect-proof nets
chemical: There is no cure for the virus. Control the whitefly vector: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3 ml/L, Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3 g/L or Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1 ml/L; rotate products
prevention: Grow barrier crops such as maize around the field

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.pathogen: Virus, spread by contact, tools and seed
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on leaves; leaves may be curled, narrow or fern-like; plants stunted; uneven fruit ripening.
organic: Remove and destroy infected plants
Wash hands and disinfect tools (e.g. with milk or 10% bleach) between plants
Do not smoke or handle tobacco near plants
chemical: No chemical cure for the virus. Focus on hygiene and removing infected plants
prevention: Use certified virus-free seed or treat seed (e.g. trisodium phosphate soak)
Rotate crops and remove crop debris

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: No disease detected. Leaves look healthy.
organic: Continue mulching, staking and compost application
prevention: Scout twice a week for whiteflies, leaf spots and blight
Water at the base in the morning
